newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Sellers slash Australian stocks by close.
newsitem.headline: Sellers slash Australian stocks by close.

text.p: SPI Futures 2477 -27 US 30yr cl 6.63 -0.08
10yrbond futs 92.670 +0.055 Gold NY 343.35 Lon fix 343.00
*Stocks close lower as traders succumb to temptation to take profits after run to record highs. Volume 433.22 million, value A$1.02 bln, 1,162 stocks traded, 324 steady, 394 up, 444 down.
The Australian share market closed lower on Friday as traders succumbed to the temptation to take profits after the run to record highs.
By 4.10 p.m. (0525 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was down 13.8 points at 2,482.6.
March share price index futures were down 27 points at 2,477, a 5.6 point discount to the index.

The day started out on a much more bullish note, however, with the benchmark All Ordinaries index hitting a record and intraday high of 2,506.5 in early trade before profit-takers pushed it down to its closing level.

"It got hit pretty hard, the SPI especially, but there was nothing in particular triggering it," said dealer Phillip Toop of Brisbane-based brokerage, Lance Jones, adding that the losses were widespread after the recent foray above the 2,500 level.
"The selling has come through across the board. CRA got hit and the banks were generally a touch softer."

Results season continued apace with Perth casino owner and operator Burswood Property Trust the first cab off the rank, reporting an 84 percent higher first half net profit of A$25.2 million. It was not enough, however, to stop its units closing four cents lower at A$1.61.

Industrial conglomerate Pacific Dunlop edged higher to A$3.16 despite a 27.6 percent lower first half net profit of A$84.46 million. Soft drink maker C-C Amatil reported a slightly higher full year net profit of A$142.1 million after trading closed. Its shares added 20.2 cents to A$13.657.

Biscuit maker Arnotts Ltd ARN.AX reported a 14.2 percent lower net profit before abnormals of A$33.2 million and its shares closed 25 cents weaker at A$8.50. However, an extortion threat that saw supermarkets remove Arnotts products from their shelves was the main news influencing the stock today, rather than the profit figure, brokers said.
Newspaper group John Fairfax Holdings reported a 24.7 percent lower first half net profit of A$46.95 million after the close. Its shares lost seven cents to A$3.03.

Mt Leyshon Gold Mines, part of the Normandy Mining, group ended unchanged at A$2.29 in thin trade after its 13.8 percent lower first half net profit of A$9.36 million. Fellow group member North Flinders Mines reported a 16.8 percent lower first half net profit of A$14.48 million, its shares ending 85 cents higher at A$7.85 after only three trades.
Falls outnumbered rises by a ratio of about nine to eight, while about 28 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Options trade was moderate while futures activity was brisk, although down on Thursday's bumper levels.
Total options traded 36,631 (48,106)
Turnover in March SPI contracts totalled 7,233 (11,220)
In other local markets, Australian bonds finished mixed as the market was quick to take profits ahead of a barrage of U.S. data later today and a U.S. holiday on Monday.

The March 10-year bond futures contract also ran into heavy resistance at 92.720, a level that kept a lid on the market during offshore trading last Friday. By 5.25 p.m. (0625 GMT), 10 year T-bonds were yielding 7.31 percent.
The Australian dollar came under renewed pressure late Friday but kept a grip on a key trendline offering the chance of an end to its 2-month downtrend.

The currency had reached as high as US$0.7730 offshore after upbeat jobs data soothed fears of another rate cut and prompted heavy short covering along with new U.S. and Swiss buying. It was slapped back by sales from a New York bank, however, and surrendered more ground as a Japanese securities house sold into strength.
By 5.50 p.m. (0650 GMT), the local currency was quoted at US$0.7641/46 down from Thursday's strong US$0.7675/80 finish.
